A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CHIMERA and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Content can be matched across relocation, renumbering, and reformatting, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V4 reports original extraction experiments, knowledge-base analyses, recombination-prediction results, and a researcher user study.

after.justification: V5 retains those empirical results and adds quantitative-biology extraction evaluation and analysis of extraction beyond seed keywords.

M1.justification: V5 adds Claude Opus 4.6 post-processing to refine extracted entity strings, storing revised fields alongside originals (Section 3.2, Appendix C.3). The original extraction and prediction methods remain, and reported experiments explicitly exclude post-processing. Appendix C.2 supplies normalization details without establishing that normalization changed.

E1.justification: V5 adds quantitative-biology abstracts as an out-of-domain extraction evaluation (Section 4.2). This extends evaluation beyond v4's AI-related abstracts while retaining the original training corpus, knowledge-base coverage, and prediction tasks.

E2.justification: The extraction comparators in Table 4, prediction methods in v4 Table 6/v5 Table 8, six user-study sources, and Appendix G comparisons are retained. Claude Opus is introduced as a post-processing component rather than an evaluated competing baseline.

E3.justification: The new domain-generalization experiment evaluates 100 quantitative-biology abstracts using the LLM-as-a-judge setup. Existing experiments retain their splits, training budgets, metrics, reranking settings, and user-study procedures. The explicit absence of keyword filtering during KB construction is newly documented, not a demonstrated protocol revision.

E4.justification: V5 adds a domain-transfer test and an audit of extraction beyond seed keywords, including keyword frequencies and examples (Section 4.2, Appendix D.1). It also briefly reports a qualitative post-processing review. Conversely, the nuanced-recombination examples shrink from five in v4 Table 17 to three in v5 Table 20, removing application-of-existing-knowledge and abstraction cases.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging five independently sampled few-shot configurations in Appendix B.2 and retain the same agreement-reporting practices. V5 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests, repeated-run counts, or other uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: V5 newly reports 94% accuracy on quantitative-biology abstracts, 3,592 recombinations (approximately 13%) from abstracts without seed keywords, and top-30 keyword counts. It adds a qualitative claim of improved post-processed entities and removes some illustrative extraction cases. The original extraction and prediction benchmark scores remain unchanged; the biological result is an added evaluation, not a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The recombination definitions and formal link-prediction task remain substantively unchanged. V5's explanation of inspiration and blend prediction clarifies existing tasks rather than introducing new mathematics, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: V5 adds biological-domain generalization to the abstract and contribution list. The central contributions—a recombination knowledge base, extraction task and annotated corpus, meta-scientific analysis, and supervised ideation—remain intact.

C2.justification: V5 interprets keyword-free extractions as evidence of generalization beyond the annotation vocabulary and the biological evaluation as domain transfer. Section 5 more explicitly bounds the demonstrated ideation approach to contextualized link prediction. Existing limitations and explanations of extraction and reranking failures are largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly specifies regex/scispaCy abbreviation handling and clustering with all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings, average linkage, and a 0.05 distance threshold. V5 also supplies the post-processing model, prompt, and disclosure of additional dataset fields. Existing code/data links and training details remain available.

R1.justification: V5 adds historical and computational positioning through Gentner (1983), Falkenhainer et al. (1989), Chan et al. (2018), and Kang et al. (2022), plus literature-based-discovery context through Sosa and Altman (2022). Several background works disappear, including Frich et al. (2019) and Youn et al. (2015). The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V5 selectively rewrites the abstract, introduction, prediction-task explanation, and conclusion. It adds appendix contents and a prompt index, expands Appendix C, and reorganizes Appendix D. The overall section sequence and most technical and appendix prose are retained.

P2.justification: V5 substantially revises presentation across the document: Figure 1 gains application panels, charts receive revised labels and sizing, Table 4 is restyled, and prediction metrics gain direction arrows. New biological and keyword tables and a post-processing prompt accompany extensive condensation and redistribution of appendix tables, including moving retained interdisciplinary examples into the main text.

improvement.justification: Compared with v4's brief normalization description, v5 provides concrete implementation steps and parameters, clarifies the prediction task, and adds limited evidence about biological and lexical generalization. These gains outweigh the removal of a few illustrative cases. The post-processing benefit remains unquantified and the new domain evaluation is narrow, so the overall improvement is limited.
